rationale: The ON state is the green track; its determinant adjacency is the white knob, not the page. Track #6cc187 vs white knob #ffffff = 2.184:1 (fail). The same track vs the dark card behind it is 6.48:1, which a page-bg-only checker would wrongly pass.
citation: "The visual information required to identify ... states ... of User Interface Components ... at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The selected-row checkmark's adjacent surface is the blue highlight row #2f6fd6, not the white page. Mark #3b6fb0 vs #2f6fd6 = 1.068:1 (fail); the same mark vs the white page is 5.14:1, which a page-bg checker would wrongly pass.
citation: "adjacent color(s)" — contrast is measured against the immediately adjacent surface, here the highlighted row, not the page. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The checked state is the white tick inside the box; its adjacent surface is the box fill #7fb0ee. Tick #ffffff vs fill #7fb0ee = 2.247:1 (fail), so the indicator that signals 'checked' is barely visible.
citation: "the visual information required to identify ... states ... requires 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors" — Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: The selected state is the inner dot; its adjacent surface is the white ring interior. Dot #b9d2f5 vs inner #ffffff = 1.544:1 (fail), so the selection is nearly invisible.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The selected tab is shown only by an underline whose adjacent surface is the blue tab strip #5a8fe0. Underline #8ab4f8 vs strip #5a8fe0 = 1.547:1 (fail); the selected state is not perceivable against the strip it sits on.
citation: "adjacent color(s)" — the underline must contrast with the strip it overlays. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: Near-threshold ON-state: green track #45b368 vs the white knob it abuts = 2.658:1, just under 3:1; the on/off state cannot be told apart from the knob edge.
citation: "at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The checked tick is rgba(255,255,255,0.5); composited over the box fill #1a73e8 it is #8db9f4, giving tick-vs-fill = 2.226:1 (fail). The runner must alpha-composite the tick against its adjacent surface before comparing.
citation: "Contrast ratio ... measured against the adjacent color(s)" — translucent indicators are composited over their backdrop. Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: An ENABLED switch in its OFF state: the OFF track #969696 vs the white page it abuts = 2.958:1 (< 3:1). The control is active, so the inactive exemption does not apply and the off-state boundary fails.
citation: "states ... of User Interface Components" must meet 3:1; only Inactive components are exempt. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 + Understanding (Exceptions)

rationale: The box fill is a gradient, so the runner cannot reduce the tick's adjacent surface to one flat color and must abstain. Truth: the pale tick #c9defb melts into the light end of the gradient, so the checked state is not perceivable along the lighter half of the box.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 — 5.1.3: "where the adjacent color is not a single solid color, determine perceivability by inspection."

rationale: The selected-tab underline sits on a busy patterned strip (photo stand-in); no flat adjacent color exists, so the runner must abstain. Truth: the light #e7eef9 underline disappears where it crosses the lighter tiles, so the selected state is not perceivable along its run.
citation: "Where the background is ... a photographic image, contrast must be evaluated against the relevant adjacent pixels." — Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: The selected dot reads against the dark outer ring border (passes) but sits in the white ring interior it actually abuts (fails). Dot #cdddf7 vs inner #ffffff = 1.374:1; the surface the indicator truly touches governs, so the selected state is not perceivable.
citation: "at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — the directly adjacent surface governs. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The selected chip is marked by a 2px inner ring whose adjacent surface is the chip's own green fill #6cc187. Ring #ffffff vs fill #6cc187 = 2.184:1 (fail), so the selected chip cannot be distinguished from the others.
citation: "the visual information required to identify ... states" must reach 3:1 against the adjacent color(s). WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: ON-state track #2e7d46 vs the white knob it abuts = 5.075:1, well above 3:1; the state is clearly perceivable.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: Adversarial near-miss: ON-track #34a853 vs the white knob = 3.056:1, just OVER 3:1, so it passes; checks that the runner's boundary direction is correct.
citation: "at least 3:1" — inclusive threshold. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The switch is disabled (aria-disabled, greyed); its ON-track #8fd6a3 vs the white knob is 1.7:1, but 1.4.11 exempts inactive/disabled components, so there is no barrier (an enabled passing switch is present as a trap).
citation: "Inactive: ... a disabled control ... is not required to meet the contrast requirements." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Exceptions)

rationale: Native checkbox and radio in their checked state with no author styling; the checked tick/dot is drawn by the browser's default user-agent stylesheet, which 1.4.11 exempts.
citation: "User Agent control: the default rendering ... is not author-controlled and is exempt." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Exceptions)

rationale: The page behind the switch is green #6cc187, so a naive page-bg checker would compare the white track to the page (2.184:1) and wrongly fail it; the determinant is the green knob #2e7d46 vs the white track = 5.075:1, which passes. Tests that the runner uses adjacency, not the page.
citation: "adjacent color(s)" — the comparison is against the indicator's adjacent surface, not the page. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: The ON-track rgba(46,125,70,0.85) composited over the white page is #4d9162 = 3.789:1 vs the white knob, above 3:1; tests that the runner composites the alpha against the known flat backdrop instead of bailing as inconclusive.
citation: "Contrast ratio ... measured against the adjacent color(s)" — composited alpha over a flat backdrop is computable. Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: The selected state is carried by the tab fill flipping to solid #1a73e8 (4.05:1 vs the #f1f3f4 strip), a sufficient perceivable cue; the faint 1px top accent #d7e3f8 is decorative garnish, not the information required to identify the state.
citation: "It does not apply to ... visual information that is not needed to identify the component." — Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: Selected dot #1a73e8 vs the white ring interior it sits in = 4.505:1, clearly perceivable; passes.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: Same gradient box fill as the abstain positive, but the tick is dark #102a52 (>=4.5:1 against the lightest gradient point), so worst-side still passes; the runner cannot reduce the gradient and should abstain while the truth is PASS.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 — 5.1.3: "determine perceivability by inspection where a single adjacent color cannot be measured."

rationale: The small selected dot has an anti-aliased circular edge against the white ring interior; a pixel-sampling runner reads blended pixels and should abstain. The author's used colors give dot #14532d vs inner #ffffff = ~9:1, a clear PASS.
citation: "Anti-aliased edges ... assessed for the intended foreground/background colors, not the blended boundary pixels." — non-text contrast measurement guidance, Understanding SC 1.4.11

rationale: Underline #1a73e8 vs the neutral strip #f1f3f4 it sits on = 4.047:1, clearly perceivable selected state; passes.
citation: "a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the adjacent color(s)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11

rationale: In a color picker each swatch is the choosable color and the near-white 'Snow' swatch #f7f7f7 has low page contrast, but presenting the true color is essential; the SELECTION indicator itself is a separate passing dark ring #303030 (>=7:1 vs the swatch), so no barrier.
citation: "Essential: A particular presentation ... is essential to the information being conveyed." — Understanding SC 1.4.11 (Exceptions)
